title: fix(plugin-list): withhold the toolbar Search on tree and chart list views (objectui#10326)
body:
Fixes #10326

Clause-②: no

Executes ruling 5825585515 (letter A): the toolbar Search is not offered on `tree` or `chart` list views, because a control that changes nothing is withheld. No new `ObjectTreeSchema` key and no search on aggregates (option B was not taken).

## What changed

`packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx`, one decision and two readers of it:

- `searchlessViewOnScreen = currentView === 'tree' || currentView === 'chart'` is declared beside `datasetChartOnScreen`, which PR objectui#10477 added for the Filter controls. It is spelled the same way.
- Reader 1 is the toolbar flag: `showSearch: ua?.search !== false && !searchlessViewOnScreen`, and the `toolbarFlags` memo lists the new primitive.
- Reader 2 is the applied term. The state is now `searchInput` / `setSearchInput`, and `searchTerm` is derived as `searchlessViewOnScreen ? '' : searchInput`. Every existing reader keeps reading `searchTerm`: the fetch (`$search`, and the client-side filter for inline data), the export, the trigger and `ganttSearchTerm`. So a term that is already set does not narrow `ListView`'s own fetch or export while a tree or chart is on screen. The typed term is kept, so switching back applies it again, and `onSearchChange` is not called for the switch.

Tests: `packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/ListView.searchWithheldTreeChart-10326.test.tsx`, 17 cases, with a stand-in registered for every view node type. Each case waits for its view's stand-in before it asserts anything.

## Mechanism assumptions, measured

- **A1 (one flag): holds.** `toolbarFlags.showSearch` is the only visibility decision. The withhold sits there, spelled the way the Filter withhold is. The applied-term gate reads the same const, so there is no second decision.
- **A2 (every chart binding): not already covered on main.** PR objectui#10477 withheld only the Filter builder and chips on a dataset-bound chart. `showSearch` was still `ua?.search !== false` there. The new const keys on `currentView === 'chart'` whatever the binding, and the pins cover both the object-bound and the dataset-bound block.
- **A3 (authored key): no key can force Search on.** Legacy `showSearch` folds into `userActions.search` in `normalizeListViewSchema`, and the flag reads `!== false`, so an authored `true` is the same as the default. On tree and chart, an authored `userActions.search: true` is now accepted and not honoured. One case pins that. No refusal or warning exists for it, and none was added. This is left as an open question in the report, the same shape PR objectui#10477 left for `userActions.filter: true` on a dataset chart.
- **A4 (carried term): it applied.** Two paths carry a term into a tree or chart view. One is `initialSearchTerm`: app-shell's `ObjectView` restores the per-view stored term through `readListFilterState`, and before this change a tree view could have stored one. The other is a switch inside one list. Both kept `$search` on `ListView`'s fetch, which feeds the record count and the export. Both are gated now and pinned.
- **A5 (other views unchanged):** Search is pinned present on kanban, calendar, gallery, timeline, map and gantt. The objectui#10250 gantt Search suite is green.

## Reverse proof (committed tree `a966cf01e`, mutation via `ablation-replace.mjs`, each leg restored to the HEAD blob with an empty `git diff HEAD`)

| leg | red | green |
|:--|:--|:--|
| both halves removed | 9: the 3 tree/chart absence cases, the 2 `userActions.search: true` cases, the 3 restored-term cases, the switch case | 8: both grid CONTROLs and the 6 other view kinds |
| visibility only (`showSearch` back to `ua?.search !== false`) | 6: the 3 absence cases, the 2 `true` cases, the switch case | 11 |
| applied term only (`searchTerm = searchInput`) | 4: the 3 restored-term cases, the switch case | 13 |

My first ablation attempt was a no-op: a shell-quoting error, exit 2, lock held 0s, nothing mutated. It was re-run through a script file, and the three rows above come from those runs.

## Changesets

- `.changeset/10326-toolbar-search-withheld-tree-chart.md`: `@object-ui/plugin-list` patch.
- `.changeset/10250-self-querying-views-toolbar-state.md` (pending): body only, frontmatter byte-identical. Its last sentence said "the toolbar Search box on `tree` and `chart` views" still does not reach those queries. That presupposes a box this change removes, so the sentence now says the box is not offered. `check-changeset-overwrite` reports this edit as its case 2 (report-only).
- `check-changeset-claims` flagged 7 pending changesets that name `ListView.tsx` (7070, 7499, 7773, 7780, 8990, list-user-actions-collision-5398, listview-comment-pair-4559). I read each paragraph: none says anything about the toolbar Search, and none is falsified. The objectui#10327 changeset is still pending and is about Filter only: still true. A wider grep of pending bodies for toolbar Search found 8317's `userActions.search !== false` fallback quote, which is still true as the default.

## Gates, all at `a966cf01e`

- vitest, targeted union of 29 files (the new file; the objectui#10250, objectui#10327, objectui#10037, 7544 and relationalSort suites; every plugin-list suite that names the toolbar search; the source-reading pins over `ListView.tsx` in app-shell, plugin-grid, types, core, react, plugin-calendar and scripts): 29 files, 875 tests passed.
- vitest `packages/plugin-list/`: 92 files, 1094 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-list type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) after the closure build (`--filter '@object-ui/plugin-list^...' build`, 12 packages): exit 0. The test project compiles the new file. An earlier run went red on a mistyped double in it, which is fixed in `a966cf01e`.
- `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check-changeset-claims`, `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` (0 new), `check-control-bytes`, `check-test-path-roots`, `check-pending-changeset-literals`, `check:unreferenced-sources`: all exit 0.
- Lint: this is a proven narrowing, not a repo-wide run. The population is what the package `lint` script lints (`eslint .` under the root `eslint.config.js`, with no package config). The eslint JSON output counts 2 files: 0 errors; `ListView.tsx` has 183 warnings, the same per-rule counts as the base blob linted through stdin, and the test file has 0. Nothing about untouched files can change: the config has no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService` (no type-aware linting), and no local rule reads other files.
- Governed-surface guard `--test` on the 4 paths: NOT GOVERNED.
- NOT MEASURED: `check:sdui-registration-pins` exited 2 with its prerequisite unmet (it needs a console build). The diff adds no registration to shipped source; the stand-ins are registered only in test scope.

## Acceptance notes

- **Boundary of the ruling (measured with a probe that was not committed).** Take a tree view on a `ListView` that has inline `data`, no `objectName` and no data source. There `ObjectTree` has no object provider and draws the host `data`, which the list's client-side search narrows. With the withhold removed, a restored term hid the non-matching row. With it, both rows are drawn and Search is absent. So on that configuration this removes a Search that did narrow the tree, though it cut the hierarchy (the triage comment names that cost). Nothing in examples, docs or apps authors a tree list view, and the console always binds `objectName` and a data source. This is raised as an open question in the report and not acted on.
- `searchableFields` on a view that is only a tree or only a chart is now read by nothing on that view. It still rides with the term once the list switches to a view that offers Search.
- The package README's "Integrated Search" bullet is still true in general. It was not edited, because it is outside the claimed file surface.
